payload.mission: Ask one question about a cultured epithelial sheet: how do cell-level motility and mechanics set the closure of a gap, and what barrier geometry results? A bounded proposal. Two published mechanics models define what is known. The Morpheus engine run here is named as a possible instrument. No wound simulation exists in this node yet.

open_questions.text: What evidence would connect a lower-scale prediction to tissue-scale closure in one named cell line? (The same shape of gap as the registered question F002.)
Is closure efficiency against gap size comparable between a Cellular Potts and a continuum model once both are calibrated to one measurement?
What barrier-geometry readout (remaining gap shape) is worth measuring beyond closed area?

requirements.text: In a declared stress-free, force-balanced model with no other active drive, setting protrusion intensity to zero leaves closed area constant to numerical tolerance. Falsified if: Closure anyway triggers diagnosis, not a presumed defect: passive relaxation, initial stress, cell-cell or cell-substrate forces or another active mechanism can legitimately close a gap. No mechanism is read from the run until the cause is found.

Closure efficiency changes with initial gap size and with protrusion intensity, as Bai and Zeng report. The abstract gives no direction, so none is assumed. Falsified if: A run that shows no dependence on either does not reproduce the reported dependence.

Paired runs from the same initial state give closed area within tolerance when dt (and grid, where there is one) is refined. Cell count is also preserved only under a declared no-birth, no-death assumption. Seed-to-seed variability is reported as an ensemble spread, not tested for equality. Falsified if: A paired change larger than the tolerance voids the comparison for that setup. Variation across independent seeds is not by itself a defect.
This project is not a clinical treatment or wound-care claim; not a viable engineered organism; not observed wound healing in any fish tissue; not evidence for fin regeneration.

What one measurement on a real construct (strain amplitude against force) would bound the model's actuation parameter?
Can the composable, scenario and refused labels of the coupling record apply to an actuation-to-motion port?

requirements.text: With actuation off, from zero initial velocity and a settled force-balanced shape, with no external flow or forcing, a defined reference frame and after a stated transient window, net displacement is zero to numerical tolerance. Falsified if: A nonzero passive displacement under those stated conditions triggers diagnosis of the setup or the runner. If a condition was not met, the control is restated, not read as a defect. No other endpoint is read until it is resolved.

Two predeclared patterns with equal total actuation give net displacements that differ by more than a dt or mesh refinement changes either one. Falsified if: If the difference is smaller than the refinement change, no pattern-to-motion statement is made.
A mirrored pattern on a symmetric body gives the mirrored displacement. Falsified if: A failure marks an anisotropy artifact in the body or the solver.
This project is not a designed living organism or a release claim; not a clinical or medical claim; not a fish tissue, or part of the flying-fish design; not frog-validated mechanics.
